newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended firmly up on Monday as the market build-up to Wednesday's budget began in earnest, dealers said.
After a bout of weakness in the morning both the all-share and industrials indices recovered and by mid-afternoon were steaming ahead.
"What we saw in the morning was just typical of a Monday morning when trade was thin. Things came right in the afternoon," one dealer said.

Dealers are braced for a volatile week as the close-out of the futures contract is fast approaching and derivatives traders are rushing to shore-up their positions, leaving the market open to steep swings.
"There was a lot of futures-related trade in the market today," one dealer said.
The all-share index ended up 29.4 points to 7,091.3 as industrials jumped 75.4 points to 8,327.0.
Most blue-chips put on modest gains including Anglos, up 100 cents to 272.00 rand, De Beers, up 100 cents to 157.50 rand and SAB, which rose 300 cents to 137.00 rand.
However, with the budget only two days away few major moves are expected before Finance Minister Trevor Manuel rises to give his budget speech in Cape Town.
All market eyes will be watching. "As yet, he (Manuel) is an unproven quantity...people will be watching very closely," said Avril Stassen, chief investor for Southern Asset Management.

"If you think about how far they (the ruling African National Congress) have come in the past five years, from nationalisation to privatisation, its quite a mind shift. This is an important budget to see what they offer." Stassen added.
The golds index fared the least well out of the three major indices on Monday as bullion woes again plagued the market.

Gold analysts are facing a topsy-turvy week as they come to terms with the news that Switzerland, hitherto the greatest champion of bullion as an asset, intends to sell over 800 tonnes of the yellow metal to establish a fund for Holocaust victims.
Gold fixed on Monday at $349.90 an ounce compared to nearly $362 a week ago and the local gold index lost 12.5 points to 1,404.4.
The futures market also had a volatile day, with early losses being replaced by late gains.
The all-share March contract last stood at 6,420/30 from 6,397 as the industrials contract was at 7,980/985 from 7,900. The golds contract was off at 975/80 from 983.
